aria: Animated recap of the Raptors' 124 to 100 home win over the Nets: Immanuel Quickley's 28-foot three with 5:33 left in the third quarter that made it 85 to 67, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Quickley's triple-double of 24 points, 10 rebounds and 14 assists, the top scorers, how the Raptors won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from Digest Sports' game page for the Raptors' 124–100 home win over Brooklyn on Nov 27, 2026, the last NBA Cup group game for both teams: all 124 Toronto points and all 100 Brooklyn points add up from the player lines. Team totals (41 of 84, 12 of 34 from three, 30 of 33 FT for Toronto; 35 of 75, 12 of 35, 18 of 24 for Brooklyn), rebounds (44–30), offensive rebounds (19–8) and assists (33–23) are on Digest Sports; the Canadian Press has Toronto's 41 of 84 and 30 of 33 and Brooklyn's 12 of 35, and Fastbreak Journal (Yardbarker) the 44–30 rebounds, 33 assists and 30 of 33. The quarter scores (31–32–39–22 to 27–28–24–21) are on Digest Sports; 63–55 at the half and 102–79 after three are also in Fastbreak Journal and VAVEL. The biggest leads (Toronto 26 at 124–98, Brooklyn 4 at 11–7) are read off Digest Sports' play-by-play. Points in the paint and bench points are not shown: no page read had them. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Immanuel Quickley had 24 points, 10 rebounds and a season-high 14 assists for a triple-double (Canadian Press; theScore), his first in four seasons with Toronto, with one turnover (Field Level Media). Scottie Barnes scored 34, his second straight 30-point game and third in five (Field Level Media). Quickley scored 16 in the third quarter, with three threes in just over a minute (Field Level Media). The win was Toronto's first at home since Oct. 28, ending a seven-game home losing streak (Field Level Media). Toronto finished 3–1 in NBA Cup group play but did not advance (Field Level Media; Canadian Press). Ja'Kobe Walter left in the third quarter with a right quad contusion; RJ Barrett and Kawhi Leonard were out (Canadian Press). Next: Brooklyn plays at Charlotte on Saturday; Toronto hosts Denver on Sunday (theScore; Canadian Press).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Immanuel Quickley's 28-foot three-pointer with 5:33 left in the third quarter that made it 85–67: Digest Sports' play-by-play has "Immanuel Quickley makes 28-foot three pointer" (no assist) at 5:33 for 82–67 to 85–67, after his threes at 6:56 and 5:57; the Canadian Press: the 28-foot three with 5:33 left capped a 13–3 run and gave Toronto an 18-point lead. So the board's Raptors +15 to +18 is 82–67 to 85–67. The defender and the spot on the floor are not described, so it is drawn with the template's plain pull-up from about 28 feet. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Toronto Raptors or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Quickley's listed 6-foot-3 and 190 pounds (Wikipedia); no wingspan was found in the sources read, so his arms are drawn at his height. He wears the Raptors' home white with No. 5 (Wikipedia). He has no look in kit/looks.json yet, so he is drawn with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
